note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Saint Lucia: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: A resident pays income tax on chargeable income at 15% on the first EC$15,000, 20% on the next EC$15,000 and 30% above EC$30,000, after a personal allowance of EC$25,000 (and other allowances); no local layer.

figures.finding: The employee pays National Insurance of 5% of gross salary up to EC$250 a month (on salary to EC$5,000), matched by the employer.

sources.said: The individual's share of National Insurance Corporation (NIC) contributions (for retirement, sickness, and disability benefits) is 5% of gross salary, up to a maximum contribution of XCD 250 per month (i.e. on a monthly salary of XCD 5,000). The employer matches the contribution and files monthly returns.

figures.finding: Employers withhold PAYE from salaries by tax code and pay it monthly; self-employed persons pay instalments on 25 March, 25 June and 25 September; resident contractors paid EC$10,000 or more have 10% withheld.

sources.said: There is withholding of tax from salaries (pay-as-you-earn or PAYE) based on tax codes obtained when employees register with the Inland Revenue Department. Tax withheld by employers is paid to the Inland Revenue on a monthly basis. Self-employed persons and individuals in partnerships are required to pay instalments by 25 March, 25 June, and 25 September.
Payments to contractors* 10 … * Contracts below XCD 10,000 are exempt from WHT.

figures.finding: A non-resident is taxed on income arising in Saint Lucia; fees and other income payments to non-residents bear 25% withholding (15% for royalties and management fees under the CARICOM agreement).

sources.said: Income arising in Saint Lucia to a non-resident
Commissions or fees (not by way of employment) 25 Income of a trust 25 Premiums, including insurance premiums 25 Any other payment of an income nature 25

figures.finding: Royalties paid to a non-resident bear 25% (15% for CARICOM residents); no resident-author regime was read.
A freelancer's fee bears VAT at 12.5% once annual turnover reaches EC$400,000; below that registration is not mandatory.

sources.said: The standard VAT rate is 12.5%. … The threshold for registered taxpayers is currently set at 400,000 East Caribbean dollars (XCD) per annum . This means that it is not mandatory for businesses earning less than the threshold to register for VAT.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; anyone with taxable income above EC$25,000 files by 31 March of the following year.

sources.said: The tax year in Saint Lucia is the calendar year. Tax returns Individuals with taxable income in excess of XCD 25,000 in any calendar year have to file a personal income tax (PIT) return by 31 March in the following year.
